Diff preload/cache identity includes workspace and whitespace mode; empty response is not completion.
Text/image size budgets and SVG display must preserve partial-result provenance.
Commit-message input with staged changes must not pretend to include unstaged/untracked changes.
Check-ignore stdin failure invokes kill/wait; verify no unreported descendant remains.
Ten-second log polling and double history traversal must meet long-history performance criteria.
A configured origin is not proof of remote access or authentication.
GitHub panel queries retain bounded lists and explicitly qualified totals.
Diff and comments are separate credential/network operations with separate failures.
Repository scan honors depth, count, excluded directories and no-follow-link policy.
Selected absolute Git roots outside workspace require their own explicit authorization.

Restore success before clean failure is not reported as an unchanged repository.
Commit with no staged files may first stage all; preserve the user-visible scope.
Commit remains real when push/sync fails and commit draft is cleared.
Every push/pull/sync fallback has its own post-state and replay policy.
Initial-commit failure retains initialized repository status and recovery instruction.
Remote repo and local origin survive later push/PATCH failure without fabricated rollback.
Invalid branch names and safe-checkout rejection do not conceal an already created branch.
Successful PR checkout refreshes branch/status/log without treating checkout as preview.
Conflicting parent worktree apply reports changed parent state despite error.
Failed initial workspace list must not be indistinguishable from an empty loaded registry.
Restore auto-connect is independent of explicit workspace selection and Git polling.
Add-many tracks candidate-level failures and successes rather than batch all-or-nothing.
Workspace persistence failure compensates newly spawned sessions but does not kill reused ones.
Clone setup/spawn/persist failure may leave disk state after best-effort cleanup.
URL clone destination cleanup failure must retain the exact attempted target and residue.
Two workspaces sharing the first live Arc must be separated by profile/auth/domain identity when required.
Removing one shared reference must not kill the process while other references survive.
Runtime-argument changes currently replace all shared keys; test selected-binding isolation.
In-flight requests and old writers remain fenced during new-spawn/map-swap/old-kill failure.
Desktop missing remote-tracking finder and daemon-provided finder are explicit non-parity branches.
Failed worktree registry write must account for created worktree and newly spawned session.
Parent removal with child errors retains an explicit partial registry and disk result.
Frontend optimistic rollback must not pretend backend in-memory settings rolled back.
Rename branch/move/persist compensation failures preserve actual disk and session path state.
Remote branch push/delete/upstream steps require separate receipts and no blind compound retry.
Remote workspace commands propagate remote failures and preserve normalized target identity.
Clone/apply/open/icon local adapters remain local despite matching daemon methods.
Windows cmd/bat and macOS open/CLI paths capture exact argv, cwd and inherited environment.
Explicit external app/command configuration is not permission for arbitrary model-selected targets.
Tilde expansion uses a product/platform resolver rather than a public dependency on Codex home.
Connected map membership must not impersonate a live child process.
